papers.study: Poupinet, Ellsworth & Fréchet (1984). Monitoring velocity variations in the crust using earthquake doublets: An application to the Calaveras Fault, California. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth.
papers.evidence: Calaveras M1.7 and M2.0 doublet around the 1979 M5.9 Coyote Lake event. Moving-window frequency-domain comparisons, approximately tenfold finer resolution than the digitisation interval, and an average S-wave velocity decrease of about 0.2% inferred for their affected paths. The teaching plot is a constructed fractional stretch, not digitised observations.

papers.study: Waldhauser & Ellsworth (2000). A Double-Difference Earthquake Location Algorithm: Method and Application to the Northern Hayward Fault, California. BSSA.
papers.evidence: 346 northern Hayward fault events. Fig. 9 compares NCSN, catalogue-difference and combined inversions. Page 1363 reports catalogue-only RMS 125 to 41 ms. Waveform P/S RMS terms in the combined inversion fell from about 96/147 to 8.5 ms each.

papers.study: Waldhauser (2001). hypoDD: A Program to Compute Double-Difference Hypocenter Locations. USGS Open-File Report 01-113.
papers.evidence: Figure 1. About 10,000 events during the 1997 Long Valley caldera sequence. Left joint hypocentre determinations, right double differences.

papers.study: Schaff, Bokelmann, Ellsworth, Zanzerkia, Waldhauser & Beroza (2004). Optimizing Correlation Techniques for Improved Earthquake Location. BSSA.
papers.evidence: 243 Calaveras lineation events. A coefficient around 0.70 and interevent separations up to about 2 km still gave better relative timing than catalogue phase data in this example.

papers.study: Trugman & Shearer (2017). GrowClust: A Hierarchical Clustering Algorithm for Relative Earthquake Relocation, with Application to the Spanish Springs and Sheldon, Nevada, Earthquake Sequences. SRL.
papers.evidence: The authors' Spanish Springs reference output contains 1,616 events. The teaching figure plots the exact same 717 events in cluster ID 1, using initial vs relocated coordinates in the corresponding rows. Cluster 1 is an example output, not a tally of the entire published swarm.

papers.study: Woods et al. (2018). Long-period seismicity reveals magma pathways above a laterally propagating dyke during the 2014–15 Bárðarbunga rifting event, Iceland. Earth and Planetary Science Letters.

Ágústsdóttir et al. (2019). Intense Seismicity During the 2014–2015 Bárðarbunga-Holuhraun Rifting Event, Iceland, Reveals the Nature of Dike-Induced Earthquakes and Caldera Collapse Mechanisms. JGR: Solid Earth.
papers.evidence: Data Set S1. 100 consecutive events starting 23 August 2014 at noon UTC, with 3-component waveforms at 11 Z7 stations used in Iceland100.

papers.study: Heimisson & Yu (2026). DDSync: Graph-Based Denoising of Differential Travel-Time Observations with Applications to Pick Reconstruction and Path-Difference Tomography. SRL.
Heimisson (2026). GraphSplit: Sparse Double-Difference Earthquake Relocation From Synchronized Differential-Time Graphs. ESS Open Archive, version 1, 2 October 2026.
papers.evidence: Title, date, status and DOI verified in the author's GraphSplit.jl README and CITATION.cff at 541f518d89bc0a2d650c7a3d0aa16485e2a6a101.
